question_record.context: A recent security incident started with a malicious email delivered to `santiago@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` and led to a series of events, including an internal phishing campaign, suspicious system hardware discovery, and eventually a renamed Windows executable being launched by a certain account.
question_record.question: Which account name was associated with the renamed and launched Windows executable?
solution: The email account `Nina Sullivan@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` received an email with a malicious URL, which was later removed.
A user account with SID `S-1-5-21-561436748-3867387497-1732241745-3701` sent phishing emails to recipients within the organization.
A suspicious system hardware discovery action was performed using `powershell.exe`.
A system executable was renamed and launched by the `SYSTEM` account.

70.name: Email messages containing malicious URL removed after delivery​
70.description: Emails with malicious URL that were delivered and later removed -V62.34.26.163

88.name: Internal phishing lexpaign
88.description: A user was observed to have sent phishing email from this device to recipients inside the organization. The user account might have been compromised in an attempt by an attacker to move laterally inside the organization. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 alert.

0.name: Suspicious System Hardware Discovery
0.description: A known tool or technique was used to gather information on this device. Attackers might be trying to gather information about the target device or network for later attacks.

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Mail_Recipient' AND o.Concept = 'Account_Derived_Email'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
